items.stem: Explain the term “a haloarene”.
items.answer: A compound in which a halogen atom is bonded directly to an sp² carbon of an aromatic ring.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a compound in which a halogen atom is bonded directly to an sp² carbon of an aromatic ring.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as gem-dihalide or vic-dihalide: dichloromethane, 1,1-dichloroethane, 2,3-dichlorobutane, 2,2-dibromopropane.
items.answer: dichloromethane – gem-dihalide; 1,1-dichloroethane – gem-dihalide; 2,3-dichlorobutane – vic-dihalide; 2,2-dibromopropane – gem-dihalide.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: dichloromethane – gem-dihalide; 1,1-dichloroethane – gem-dihalide; 2,3-dichlorobutane – vic-dihalide; 2,2-dibromopropane – gem-dihalide.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): C–X bond length increases from C–F to C–I.
Reason (R): C–X bond enthalpy increases from C–F to C–I.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It decreases from C–F to C–I as bond length increases.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ethylidene chloride is 1,2-dichloroethane.”
items.answer: Ethylidene chloride is 1,1-dichloroethane; ethylene dichloride is 1,2-dichloroethane.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Ethylidene chloride is 1,1-dichloroethane; ethylene dichloride is 1,2-dichloroethane.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The C–X bond in haloalkanes is polar.
Reason (R): Halogens are more electronegative than carbon.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Carbon carries δ⁺, halogen δ⁻.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Kavya examines the compounds CH₃CH₂Cl, CH₂=CHCl and C₆H₅Cl.
(i) Classify each. (1 mark)
(ii) Which has the longest C–Cl bond? Why? (2 marks)
(iii) Which carbon hybridisation is present in the C–Cl bond of chloroethane? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Chloroethane: 1° alkyl halide; CH₂=CHCl: vinylic; C₆H₅Cl: aryl. (ii) Chloroethane: in vinyl and aryl chlorides resonance gives partial double bond character and the carbon is sp², shortening the bond. (iii) sp³.

items.stem: Write the structures of all isomers of C₄H₉Br and classify each as 1°, 2° or 3°.
items.answer: 1-Bromobutane (1°), 2-bromobutane (2°), 1-bromo-2-methylpropane (1°), 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (3°).
items.markingKey: 1 mark structures; 1 mark classification.

items.stem: Which of the following is a vic-dihalide?
items.answer: 2,3-dichlorobutane
items.markingKey: (b) 2,3-dichlorobutane is a vic-dihalide; the others are not.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of C–X bond length: C–I, C–Br, C–F, C–Cl. Give a reason.
items.answer: C–F < C–Cl < C–Br < C–I
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order C–F < C–Cl < C–Br < C–I; 1 mark for the reason: Bond length increases as the size of the halogen increases.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(Br)CH₃?
items.answer: 2-bromobutane
items.markingKey: (b) CH₃CH₂CH(Br)CH₃ = 2-bromobutane (lowest locants; substituents in alphabetical order).

items.stem: Write the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(Cl)CH₂CH₃.
items.answer: 2-Chlorobutane.
items.markingKey: 1 mark.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a vic-dihalide?
items.answer: 2-bromobutane
items.markingKey: (a) 2-bromobutane is a monohalide, not a vic-dihalide.

items.stem: Define the term “Lucas reagent”.
items.answer: Concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂, used to convert alcohols to chlorides and to distinguish 1°, 2° and 3° alcohols.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂, used to convert alcohols to chlorides and to distinguish 1°, 2° and 3° alcohols.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about preparation and physical properties of haloalkanes is correct?
items.answer: Boiling points of alkyl halides increase in the order RF < RCl < RBr < RI.
items.markingKey: (a) Boiling points of alkyl halides increase in the order RF < RCl < RBr < RI. The other statements are false. Branching lowers the surface area and van der Waals forces, so the boiling point decreases. They cannot form strong hydrogen bonds with water, so they are only slightly soluble. Alkyl fluorides are formed using AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂ or SbF₃.
options: Boiling points of alkyl halides increase in the order RF < RCl < RBr < RI.
In the Swarts reaction alkyl iodides are formed.
Branching increases the boiling point of isomeric haloalkanes.
Haloalkanes are highly soluble in water.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): p-Dichlorobenzene has a higher melting point than o- and m-isomers.
Reason (R): Haloalkanes are highly soluble in water.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: They cannot form strong hydrogen bonds with water, so they are only slightly soluble.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Branching increases the boiling point of isomeric haloalkanes.”
items.answer: Branching lowers the surface area and van der Waals forces, so the boiling point decreases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Branching lowers the surface area and van der Waals forces, so the boiling point decreases.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): p-Dichlorobenzene has a higher melting point than o-dichlorobenzene.
Reason (R): The para isomer is more symmetrical and fits better in the crystal lattice.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Better packing.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Manish compares the boiling points of CH₃Cl (249 K), CH₃Br (276 K), CH₃I (316 K) and of the isomers of C₄H₉Br.
(i) Why does the boiling point rise from CH₃Cl to CH₃I? (1 mark)
(ii) Arrange 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane by boiling point. (2 marks)
(iii) Why are haloalkanes heavier than water? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Molecular mass and polarisability increase, so van der Waals forces increase. (ii) 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane < 2-bromobutane < 1-bromobutane; branching lowers surface area. (iii) Halogen atoms have high atomic mass, so bromo and iodo compounds are denser than water.

items.stem: Which of the following is a method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols?
items.answer: HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂
items.markingKey: (d) HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂ is a method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols; the others are not.

items.stem: Write the equation for the Finkelstein reaction and explain why it goes to completion.
items.answer: CH₃CH₂Br + NaI → CH₃CH₂I + NaBr (in dry acetone). NaBr is insoluble in acetone and precipitates, which shifts the equilibrium forward (Le Chatelier).
items.markingKey: 1 mark equation; 1 mark reason.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about preparation and physical properties of haloalkanes is incorrect?
items.answer: Branching increases the boiling point of isomeric haloalkanes.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Branching increases the boiling point of isomeric haloalkanes.” Correct form: Branching lowers the surface area and van der Waals forces, so the boiling point decreases.
options: Branching increases the boiling point of isomeric haloalkanes.
Density increases with the number and atomic mass of halogen atoms.
Among isomeric alkyl halides, boiling point decreases with branching.
p-Dichlorobenzene has a higher melting point than o- and m-isomers.

items.stem: What is the main organic product when propene is treated with HBr?
items.answer: 2-bromopropane
items.markingKey: (b) 2-bromopropane: Markovnikov's addition.
options: a mixture of o- and p-chlorotoluene

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of density: CHCl₃, CH₂Cl₂, CCl₄. Give a reason.
items.answer: CH₂Cl₂ < CHCl₃ < CCl₄
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order CH₂Cl₂ < CHCl₃ < CCl₄; 1 mark for the reason: Density increases with number of chlorine atoms.

items.stem: Which term describes the preparation of alkyl fluorides by heating alkyl chlorides or bromides with metallic fluorides such as AgF or Hg₂F₂?
items.answer: the Swarts reaction
items.markingKey: (c) The Swarts reaction: the preparation of alkyl fluorides by heating alkyl chlorides or bromides with metallic fluorides such as AgF or Hg₂F₂.

items.stem: What is meant by “a Grignard reagent”?
items.answer: An alkylmagnesium halide RMgX, made from an alkyl halide and Mg in dry ether.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an alkylmagnesium halide RMgX, made from an alkyl halide and Mg in dry ether.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about reactions of haloalkanes and haloarenes is correct?
items.answer: Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution.
items.markingKey: (b) Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution. The other statements are false. Tertiary halides form the most stable carbocations and react fastest by SN1; primary halides prefer SN2. It needs NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm (Dow process). With KCN they give nitriles; AgCN gives isocyanides.
options: Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution.
Primary alkyl halides react fastest by the SN1 mechanism.
Chlorobenzene readily gives phenol with aqueous NaOH at room temperature.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Haloalkanes give isocyanides with KCN.
Reason (R): SN2 reactions occur with inversion of configuration.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: With KCN they give nitriles; AgCN gives isocyanides. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Primary alkyl halides react fastest by the SN1 mechanism.”
items.answer: Tertiary halides form the most stable carbocations and react fastest by SN1; primary halides prefer SN2.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Tertiary halides form the most stable carbocations and react fastest by SN1; primary halides prefer SN2.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): KCN gives alkyl cyanides while AgCN gives isocyanides with haloalkanes.
Reason (R): KCN is ionic and attacks through C; AgCN is covalent so N attacks.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Ambident cyanide.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Give two differences between β-elimination (E2) and SN1.
items.answer: β-elimination (E2): H and X lost from adjacent carbons; strong base such as alcoholic KOH. SN1: two steps via a carbocation; rate = k[RX].
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. β-elimination (E2) – H and X lost from adjacent carbons; strong base such as alcoholic KOH; SN1 – two steps via a carbocation; rate = k[RX].

items.stem:
A substitution mechanism has these features: fastest for CH₃X and 1° halides; rate = k[RX][Nu⁻]; one step, no intermediate.
(i) Identify the mechanism. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were SN1? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) SN2 (ii) inversion of configuration (iii) two steps via a carbocation; racemisation of an optically active substrate
items.markingKey: (i) SN2 – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: inversion of configuration – 1 mark. (iii) for SN1: two steps via a carbocation; rate = k[RX]; racemisation of an optically active substrate – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between β-elimination (E2) and SN2 on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A substitution mechanism has these features: rate = k[RX][Nu⁻]. Identify the mechanism – β-elimination (E2) or SN2? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) β-elimination (E2): strong base such as alcoholic KOH; H and X lost from adjacent carbons; alkene formed. SN2: one step, no intermediate; rate = k[RX][Nu⁻]; inversion of configuration. (b) SN2.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: SN2; 1 mark: “rate = k[RX][Nu⁻]” is a feature of SN2.

items.stem: Which term describes a two-step unimolecular nucleophilic substitution through a carbocation intermediate?
items.answer: an SN1 reaction
items.markingKey: (b) An SN1 reaction: a two-step unimolecular nucleophilic substitution through a carbocation intermediate.

items.stem: Why is chlorobenzene less reactive than chloroethane towards nucleophilic substitution? Give two reasons.
items.answer: (i) Resonance gives the C–Cl bond partial double bond character, making it hard to break. (ii) The carbon is sp² hybridised, more electronegative, giving a shorter, stronger bond; also the electron-rich ring repels the nucleophile and the phenyl cation is unstable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each reason.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of reactivity towards SN1: CH₃Br, (CH₃)₂CHBr, (CH₃)₃CBr, CH₃CH₂Br. Give a reason.
items.answer: (CH₃)₃CBr > (CH₃)₂CHBr > CH₃CH₂Br > CH₃Br
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order (CH₃)₃CBr > (CH₃)₂CHBr > CH₃CH₂Br > CH₃Br; 1 mark for the reason: Carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl.

items.stem: A substitution mechanism has these features: H and X lost from adjacent carbons; strong base such as alcoholic KOH. Identify the mechanism. Give a reason.
items.answer: β-elimination (E2)
items.markingKey: 1 mark: β-elimination (E2); 1 mark: the features H and X lost from adjacent carbons; strong base such as alcoholic KOH are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Explain the SN1 and SN2 mechanisms with suitable examples. How do the structure of the alkyl halide and the stereochemistry of the product differ in the two cases?
items.answer: SN2: e.g. CH₃Cl + OH⁻; one step, backside attack through a pentacoordinate transition state; rate = k[RX][OH⁻]; inversion; reactivity CH₃ > 1° > 2° > 3°. SN1: e.g. (CH₃)₃CBr + OH⁻; slow ionisation to carbocation, then fast attack; rate = k[RX]; racemisation of chiral substrates; reactivity 3° > 2° > 1°; favoured by polar protic solvents.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each mechanism; 1 mark comparison.

items.stem: Write the product and name the type of reaction when chlorobenzene is treated with sodium and CH₃Cl in dry ether.
items.answer: Toluene; Wurtz–Fittig reaction
items.markingKey: Product: toluene (1); Wurtz–Fittig reaction (1).

items.stem: What is the main organic product when bromobenzene reacts with sodium in dry ether?
items.answer: biphenyl
items.markingKey: (d) biphenyl: Fittig reaction.

items.stem: Define the term “enantiomers”.
items.answer: Stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about stereochemistry: optical isomerism and chirality is correct?
items.answer: Butan-2-ol is chiral.
items.markingKey: (c) Butan-2-ol is chiral. The other statements are false. Its C-2 carries two identical CH₃ groups, so it is achiral. SN2 reactions proceed with inversion (Walden inversion). Enantiomers have identical physical properties except the sign of rotation.
options: SN2 reactions proceed with retention of configuration.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a description of a racemic mixture?
items.markingKey: (−) is a laevorotatory label, not a description of a racemic mixture.

items.stem: Identify the chiral molecule in the pair 2-chlorobutane and 1-chlorobutane, and mark the asymmetric carbon.
items.answer: 2-Chlorobutane is chiral; C-2 (bearing H, Cl, CH₃ and C₂H₅) is the asymmetric carbon. 1-Chlorobutane has no such carbon.
items.markingKey: 1 mark identification; 1 mark asymmetric carbon.

items.stem: Which of the following compounds is NOT chiral?
items.answer: 1-bromobutane
items.markingKey: (c) 1-bromobutane has no carbon bonded to four different groups.

items.stem:
Ishaan places a solution of an organic compound in a polarimeter and finds that it rotates plane-polarised light to the left. The compound is C₄H₉Br.
(i) Which isomer is it? (1 mark)
(ii) What label is used for leftward rotation? (1 mark)
(iii) What would be observed if an equal amount of its mirror image were mixed in, and what is this mixture called? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 2-Bromobutane (the only chiral isomer of C₄H₉Br). (ii) Laevorotatory, (−) or l. (iii) Zero rotation; a racemic mixture.

items.stem: Pure (+)-2-chlorobutane has a specific rotation of +36.0°. A sample of it prepared by Sneha shows a specific rotation of +10.8°. Calculate the optical purity (enantiomeric excess) and the percentage of each enantiomer.
items.markingKey: Optical purity = observed/pure × 100 = 10.8/36.0 × 100 = 30% (1); (+) = 50 + ee/2 = 65%, (−) = 35% (the rest is racemic) (2).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “A racemic mixture rotates plane-polarised light to the right.”
items.answer: The rotations of the two enantiomers cancel; it is optically inactive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The rotations of the two enantiomers cancel; it is optically inactive.

items.stem: Which of the following is a laevorotatory label?

items.stem: Which of the following statements about stereochemistry: optical isomerism and chirality is incorrect?

items.answer: COCl₂, the highly poisonous gas formed when chloroform is oxidised by air in light.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄) and freon-12 (CCl₂F₂) on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A polyhalogen compound has these features: reaches the stratosphere unchanged. Identify the compound – carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄) or freon-12 (CCl₂F₂)? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄): used to make refrigerants and propellants; earlier used in fire extinguishers; can damage the liver. Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂): used in refrigeration and air conditioning; very stable and non-toxic; reaches the stratosphere unchanged. (b) Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: freon-12 (CCl₂F₂); 1 mark: “reaches the stratosphere unchanged” is a feature of freon-12 (CCl₂F₂).

items.stem: A substitution mechanism has these features: one step, no intermediate; inversion of configuration. Identify the mechanism. Give a reason.
items.answer: SN2
items.markingKey: 1 mark: SN2; 1 mark: the features one step, no intermediate; inversion of configuration are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method of preparing haloarenes?
items.answer: HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂
items.markingKey: (d) HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂ is a method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols, not a method of preparing haloarenes.

items.stem: Which term describes a compound in which the halogen is bonded to an sp² carbon of a C=C double bond?
items.answer: a vinylic halide
items.markingKey: (a) A vinylic halide: a compound in which the halogen is bonded to an sp² carbon of a C=C double bond.

items.stem: Write the product and name the type of reaction when bromoethane is treated with AgNO₂.
items.answer: Nitroethane (CH₃CH₂NO₂); the covalent AgNO₂ attacks through nitrogen
items.markingKey: Product: nitroethane (CH₃CH₂NO₂) (1); the covalent AgNO₂ attacks through nitrogen (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a use of dichloromethane?
items.answer: solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine
items.markingKey: (c) Solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine is a use of chloroform, not a use of dichloromethane.
options: solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “SN2 reactions proceed with retention of configuration.”
items.answer: SN2 reactions proceed with inversion (Walden inversion).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: SN2 reactions proceed with inversion (Walden inversion).

items.stem:
A polyhalogen compound has these features: formed from ethanol or propanone with I₂ and NaOH; antiseptic action due to liberated iodine; unpleasant smell.
(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were chloroform (CHCl₃)? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Iodoform (CHI₃) (ii) yellow solid (iii) oxidised in light to phosgene; earlier used as an anaesthetic
items.markingKey: (i) iodoform (CHI₃) – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: yellow solid – 1 mark. (iii) for chloroform (CHCl₃): solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine; earlier used as an anaesthetic; oxidised in light to phosgene – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about classification, nomenclature and the C–X bond is correct?
items.answer: The C–X bond is polar, with carbon carrying a partial positive charge.
items.markingKey: (d) The C–X bond is polar, with carbon carrying a partial positive charge. The other statements are false. It decreases from C–F to C–I as bond length increases. It is bonded to an sp² carbon; CH₂=CHCl is a vinylic halide. Ethylidene chloride is 1,1-dichloroethane; ethylene dichloride is 1,2-dichloroethane.
options: C–X bond enthalpy increases from C–F to C–I.
In CH₂=CHCl the halogen is bonded to an sp³ carbon.
The C–X bond is polar, with carbon carrying a partial positive charge.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane by SN1 gives an optically inactive product.
Reason (R): The planar carbocation is attacked equally from both faces.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Racemisation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of reactivity towards SN2: (CH₃)₂CHBr, CH₃Br, CH₃CH₂Br. Give a reason.
items.answer: CH₃Br > CH₃CH₂Br > (CH₃)₂CHBr
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order CH₃Br > CH₃CH₂Br > (CH₃)₂CHBr; 1 mark for the reason: Steric hindrance to backside attack increases from methyl to tertiary.

items.stem: Explain the term “the Sandmeyer reaction”.
items.answer: The replacement of the diazonium group by Cl or Br using CuCl/HCl or CuBr/HBr.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the replacement of the diazonium group by Cl or Br using CuCl/HCl or CuBr/HBr.

items.stem: Classify p-ClC₆H₄CH₃.
items.answer: an aryl halide
items.markingKey: (b) p-ClC₆H₄CH₃ is an aryl halide.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of boiling point of isomers?
items.answer: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane < 2-bromobutane < 1-bromobutane
items.markingKey: (b) 2-bromo-2-methylpropane < 2-bromobutane < 1-bromobutane. More branching ⇒ smaller surface area ⇒ lower boiling point.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as halogen exchange method or method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols: SOCl₂, Swarts reaction, Finkelstein reaction, HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂.
items.answer: SOCl₂ – method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols; Swarts reaction – halogen exchange method; Finkelstein reaction – halogen exchange method; HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂ – method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: SOCl₂ – method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols; Swarts reaction – halogen exchange method; Finkelstein reaction – halogen exchange method; HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂ – method of preparing haloalkanes from alcohols.

items.stem: Which term describes an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers, showing zero optical rotation?
items.answer: a racemic mixture
items.markingKey: (a) A racemic mixture: an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers, showing zero optical rotation.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “C–X bond enthalpy increases from C–F to C–I.”
items.answer: It decreases from C–F to C–I as bond length increases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It decreases from C–F to C–I as bond length increases.

items.stem:
A substitution mechanism has these features: alkene formed; strong base such as alcoholic KOH; major product follows Zaitsev's rule.
(i) Identify the mechanism. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were SN1? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) β-elimination (E2) (ii) H and X lost from adjacent carbons (iii) rate = k[RX]; fastest for 3° halides, favoured by polar protic solvents
items.markingKey: (i) β-elimination (E2) – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: H and X lost from adjacent carbons – 1 mark. (iii) for SN1: two steps via a carbocation; rate = k[RX]; racemisation of an optically active substrate – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “DDT is rapidly broken down in the environment.”
items.answer: DDT is very persistent and is stored in fatty tissues, leading to biomagnification.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: DDT is very persistent and is stored in fatty tissues, leading to biomagnification.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Chloroform is stored in closed dark coloured bottles filled to the brim.
Reason (R): The smell of iodoform is pleasant, so it is still used widely.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Its unpleasant smell led to its replacement by other iodine formulations.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄) and DDT on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A polyhalogen compound has these features: can damage the liver. Identify the compound – carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄) or DDT? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄): used to make refrigerants and propellants; earlier used in fire extinguishers; can damage the liver. DDT: first chlorinated organic insecticide; used against malaria-carrying mosquitoes; not biodegradable. (b) Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄); 1 mark: “can damage the liver” is a feature of carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄).

items.stem: A substitution mechanism has these features: fastest for CH₃X and 1° halides; one step, no intermediate; inversion of configuration. Identify the mechanism. Give a reason.
items.answer: SN2
items.markingKey: 1 mark: SN2; 1 mark: the features fastest for CH₃X and 1° halides; one step, no intermediate; inversion of configuration are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method of preparing haloarenes?
items.answer: Finkelstein reaction
items.markingKey: (d) Finkelstein reaction is a halogen exchange method, not a method of preparing haloarenes.

items.stem: Which term describes a compound in which a halogen atom is bonded to an sp³ hybridised carbon of an alkyl group?
items.answer: a haloalkane
items.markingKey: (b) A haloalkane: a compound in which a halogen atom is bonded to an sp³ hybridised carbon of an alkyl group.

items.stem: Write the product and name the type of reaction when bromobenzene is treated with sodium in dry ether.
items.answer: Biphenyl; Fittig reaction
items.markingKey: Product: biphenyl (1); Fittig reaction (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a use of carbon tetrachloride (earlier or current)?
items.answer: propellant in aerosols
items.markingKey: (a) Propellant in aerosols is a use of dichloromethane, not a use of carbon tetrachloride (earlier or current).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “2-Bromopropane is chiral.”
items.answer: Its C-2 carries two identical CH₃ groups, so it is achiral.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Its C-2 carries two identical CH₃ groups, so it is achiral.

items.stem:
A polyhalogen compound has these features: antiseptic action due to liberated iodine; unpleasant smell; formed from ethanol or propanone with I₂ and NaOH.
(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were freon-12 (CCl₂F₂)? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Iodoform (CHI₃) (ii) yellow solid (iii) used in refrigeration and air conditioning; very stable and non-toxic
items.markingKey: (i) iodoform (CHI₃) – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: yellow solid – 1 mark. (iii) for freon-12 (CCl₂F₂): used in refrigeration and air conditioning; very stable and non-toxic; reaches the stratosphere unchanged – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about classification, nomenclature and the C–X bond is correct?
items.answer: C–X bond length increases from C–F to C–I.
items.markingKey: (c) C–X bond length increases from C–F to C–I. The other statements are false. It decreases from C–F to C–I as bond length increases. It is bonded to an sp² carbon; CH₂=CHCl is a vinylic halide. Ethylidene chloride is 1,1-dichloroethane; ethylene dichloride is 1,2-dichloroethane.
options: In CH₂=CHCl the halogen is bonded to an sp³ carbon.
C–X bond length increases from C–F to C–I.
C–X bond enthalpy increases from C–F to C–I.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): 2-Bromobutane is optically active.
Reason (R): It contains a carbon atom bonded to four different groups.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) C-2 bears H, Br, CH₃ and C₂H₅.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of reactivity towards SN1: CH₃CH₂Br, CH₃Br, (CH₃)₂CHBr. Give a reason.
items.answer: (CH₃)₂CHBr > CH₃CH₂Br > CH₃Br
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order (CH₃)₂CHBr > CH₃CH₂Br > CH₃Br; 1 mark for the reason: Carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl.

items.stem: Explain the term “the Finkelstein reaction”.
items.answer: The preparation of alkyl iodides by treating alkyl chlorides or bromides with NaI in dry acetone.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the preparation of alkyl iodides by treating alkyl chlorides or bromides with NaI in dry acetone.

items.stem: Classify CH₃CH₂Cl.
items.answer: a primary (1°) alkyl halide
items.markingKey: (a) CH₃CH₂Cl is a primary (1°) alkyl halide.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of density?
items.answer: CH₂Cl₂ < CHCl₃ < CCl₄
items.markingKey: (d) CH₂Cl₂ < CHCl₃ < CCl₄. Density increases with number of chlorine atoms.
